featured_videos.title: Got On The Scale & Here's Where I'm At: LIFE UPDATE
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.editorial_title: Got On The Scale & Here's Where I'm At: LIFE UPDATE
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here are hitting different because nobody's pretending the scale is the whole story. You've got people celebrating 97 pounds lost while admitting they added potatoes back in. You've got someone who fell off for months, got back on, and dropped 11 pounds in a week. That's the real conversation the carnivore community actually needs, and Cassie's honesty is opening it up. The struggle isn't about perfect compliance, it's about knowing you can always come back, and that's way more powerful than any single weigh-in number.

featured_videos.title: These Carnivore Meatballs Shouldn't Be This Good
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: These Carnivore Meatballs Shouldn't Be This Good
featured_videos.commentary: What I love about this is the comments. people are already improvising. Ground beef instead of sausage, dry ranch seasoning, air fryer instead of pan. That's the carnivore sweet spot, right there. You don't need fancy plating or perfect technique to make something work for your life. Cheese-bound meatballs are one of those recipes that stick around because they're forgiving, they're filling, and honestly, they taste better than they have any right to. If you're tired of seeing "carnivore recipes" loaded with plant-based binders, this is the reset you needed.

featured_videos.title: It Took Me 3 Years on Carnivore to Realize What I'll Tell You in 15 Minutes
featured_videos.creator: Max German
featured_videos.editorial_title: It Took Me 3 Years on Carnivore to Realize What I'll Tell You in 15 Minutes
featured_videos.commentary: Max nailed something the community keeps circling back to: three years in, you finally stop white-knuckling the "rules" and start listening to your body. The comment about coffee flushing electrolytes? That's the kind of detail people miss in week one when they're just trying to survive the transition. And there's real wisdom in that 76-year-old's comment too, because he's not talking about some miracle cure, just "best decision of my life". which is how most people actually experience this. The electrolyte thing especially matters because so many people blame carnivore for fatigue when really they're just depleted, and a few tweaks with salt and minerals flips everything. What Max is doing here is stripping away the dogma and showing what sustainability actually looks like after the honeymoon phase wears off.

featured_videos.title: For 4 YEARS my almost DAILY, CHEAP, & FAVORITE Carnivore Meal is?
featured_videos.creator: Mitch Weiss, OGC, Healthy Aging
featured_videos.editorial_title: For 4 YEARS my almost DAILY, CHEAP, & FAVORITE Carnivore Meal is?
featured_videos.commentary: That cholesterol comment though. this is exactly what people need to see. You can eat bacon and eggs almost daily for four years, hit textbook-perfect lipid numbers, and doctors *still* push back. It's frustrating because the data's right there. The real win in Mitch's video isn't just the meal itself, it's the proof that simple, repetitive eating works. No complexity, no overthinking. And the chaffle riffs in the comments show how easy it is to build on this foundation when you're actually craving something more substantial. That's the opposite of diet fatigue.

featured_videos.title: @DoctorMike Doesn't Know What Food Is
featured_videos.creator: Kent Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: The community's calling out what we all see here: mainstream doctors often don't actually know what they're talking about when it comes to real nutrition. Dr. Mike's shopping cart is basically what the food industry *wants* people to buy, not what their bodies actually need. The gap between "recommended by a doctor" and "actually healthy" has gotten so wide that people are rightfully skeptical. That said, the comment about oxalates is worth noting. berries and kiwis aren't the nutritional slam dunk most people think they are, especially if you're dealing with inflammation or joint issues. The real takeaway? Your own results matter infinitely more than a credential or a shopping vlog.

featured_videos.title: A New Review Warns Against The CARNIVORE Diet
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: A New Review Warns Against The CARNIVORE Diet
featured_videos.commentary: The comments on this one tell you everything. Someone who couldn't walk two years ago just went tubing, dropped 70 pounds, and cut their insulin in half, and the response isn't "tell me more about your protocol" but rather "the system profits from keeping you sick." That's not anti-science. That's lived experience bumping up against a research scene that's barely caught up to what people are actually achieving. Dr. Hampton nails it when he says nine human studies should make us curious, not tribal. The real conversation isn't whether carnivore is perfect or dangerous, it's why we're still asking basic questions about a way of eating that's been healing people faster than the literature can measure.
